stem: A nurse is preparing to discontinue Transmission-Based Precautions for a client whose infectious diagnosis is now known. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Use the organism- or condition-specific duration criteria in current CDC guidance and applicable facility or public-health requirements rather than applying one fixed isolation period to every infection
options.B: Discontinue precautions after the same 24-hour period for every infectious diagnosis regardless of transmission risk
options.C: Require negative cultures for every infectious disease before any Transmission-Based Precautions can be stopped
options.D: Continue all Transmission-Based Precautions indefinitely because infectious shedding cannot be estimated clinically

rationale: CDC states that Transmission-Based Precautions remain in effect while transmission risk persists or for the recommended duration of illness, and Appendix A provides disease-specific type and duration guidance. Some conditions use a defined treatment interval, others the duration of illness, and selected infections use microbiologic clearance or additional jurisdictional criteria. No single time or universal negative-test rule applies to all pathogens.
educational_objective: Use pathogen-specific CDC duration criteria when deciding when Transmission-Based Precautions can be discontinued.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_document_title: Guideline for Isolation Precautions — Appendix A: Type and Duration of Precautions; Precautions to Prevent Transmission
source_version_date: Appendix A updated February 7, 2025; current guidance accessed 2026
source_locator: Part III: precautions remain while transmission risk persists or for duration of illness; Appendix A lists infection-specific types/durations and exceptions including treatment- or test-based criteria
source_claim_supported: Duration of Transmission-Based Precautions is pathogen/condition specific; universal fixed-time or negative-test rules are inappropriate.

correction_summary: Removed the source's pseudo-universal list of symptom resolution, treatment completion, or negative tests. Rebuilt around CDC's explicit pathogen-specific duration framework and jurisdiction/facility exceptions.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: CDC Appendix A and Part III duration guidance verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Pathogen-specific duration, selective test-based criteria and no universal fixed duration are supported.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A reflects CDC's disease-specific framework.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked TB/state-law exceptions, immunocompromised prolonged shedding, treatment-based diseases and test-based exceptions; no unresolved conflict.
